proof:
Put $B=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and choose $z_0\in\operatorname{relint}B\cap\mathbb Z^n$. It belongs to $P$ by lattice completeness, and it can be expressed using all sites in $P$ with strictly positive weights. Indeed, if $\bar z$ is their average, then $(z_0-t\bar z)/(1-t)$ is in $B$ for small positive $t$, and any convex representation of that point gives the required representation after adding $t\bar z$. Incidence rigidity from joint-measure-homothetic-domination-and-strata yields the common tangent space $V$. That lemma also gives exact integer fibers $S_z$ for $D=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times S_z)$.

Choose $y\in\operatorname{relint}D$ and let $p$ be its base. Since $z_0$ lies in $\operatorname{relint}B$, there is a point $p'\in B$ such that $z_0$ is a convex combination of $p$ and $p'$ with positive weight on $p$. Choose a point of $D$ over $p'$ and take the same combination with $y$. The combination is in $\operatorname{relint}D$, because a relative ball about $y$ shrinks by a positive factor in the combination. It is over $z_0$. Consequently the direction of the section $D_{z_0}$ is the vertical kernel of $\operatorname{aff}(D)$ under projection to the base. Since $D_{z_0}=S_{z_0}$, this kernel is $V$. It follows that the perpendicular projection to $V^\perp$ of a point of $\operatorname{aff}(D)$ depends only on its base and is affine there. Call that map $b$. The shear and its inverse are affine, and on each fiber the shear is a translation, proving the asserted invariances.
statement: Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu_z$ be nonzero finite positive Borel measures of compact support $S_z\subset\mathbb R^D$ indexed by a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$. Suppose every combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$, $\theta_i>0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies $\mu_z(\sum_i\theta_i E_i)^{1/N}\ge\sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}$ for compact positive-mass $E_i$. If $\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$ contains an integer point, then all supports have a common tangent space $V$. There is an affine map $b:\operatorname{aff}(P)\to V^\perp$ such that $S_z\subseteq b(z)+V$ for every $z\in P$. The hull of the placed supports has exactly those integer fibers. The affine shear $(z,x)\mapsto(z,x-b(z))$ fixes bases, preserves intrinsic fiber measure, and carries affine halfspaces to affine halfspaces in the space over $\operatorname{aff}(P)$.
title: A relative-interior integer base forces an affine support graph
